text:
alex: heads-up — seeing a spike in 429s for EU prod since the rate limit rollout around 12:03 UTC. multiple customer tickets about timeouts + billing alerts. :rotating_light:
sara: same here. dashboard shows 429s up ~8x and tail latency creeping. correlated with policy deploy c3f4a. link: https://internal.redwood/changes/c3f4a :eyes:
matt: can someone paste the policy diff? curious what changed for burst handling.
sara: diff attached (abbreviated):
```yaml
policy_id: core-rate-2026-06
tiers:
  free:
    rate_per_minute: 9000
    burst_limit: 50    # lowered from 200
    token_bucket_window_ms: 1000
  paid:
    rate_per_minute: 60000
    burst_limit: 1000
```
jia: lowering burst_limit to 50 will absolutely throttle short high-throughput syncs. sounds like the scheduled ETL jobs + a few SDK customers hit the bucket. repro steps I ran locally:
```bash
# reproducible locally against staging policy mirror
for i in {1..120}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"ping"}' &
done;
# you'll see 200s then 429s after ~50 requests in <1s
```
support-bot: ticket ACME-11234 escalated: heavy sync job gets 429s intermittently, customer saw billing spike from retries. Support asked for ETA on fix.
alex: my recommendation: pause this policy rollout in EU and rollback to previous burst_limit until we add a canary test for bursty jobs. we should also coordinate comms with billing to avoid charging for automated retry loops. @matt, you're infra oncall?
matt: oncall yes. I'll roll back. plan:
1) revert commit c3f4a in policy repo (git revert c3f4a)
2) push config to policy-service: `kubectl apply -f policies/core-rate-rollback.yaml`
3) restart policy-manager deployment if needed: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/policy-manager -n redwood-mgmt`
4) validate using prometheus queries and run the repro script from staging
5) notify support + product

deploy-bot: started deployment revert for policies/core-rate at 12:38:21 UTC (deploy-id: revert-1782345678)
sara: FYI we also saw a flurry from a third-party integrator hitting a cached endpoint concurrently. lowering burst_limit without throttling for specific routes was risky.
matt: rollback completed in EU at 12:41 UTC. initial metrics: 429 rate dropped from ~95/min to ~6/min within 3 minutes. latency returned to baseline.
support-bot: updated ACME-11234 with status: rollback applied, monitoring. asked customer to pause retries and we suppressed billing events for the window.
alex: thanks. immediate follow-ups:
- jia: capture exact repro script + synthetic test and add to canary suite (owner: jia)
- sara: propose safer defaults for burst_limit and route-level exceptions; write policy PR with rationale (owner: sara)
- matt: add a deployment gate that runs bursty canaries before enabling on EU/NA (owner: matt)
- product: prepare short customer-facing note and coordinate with billing ops (owner: alex)

jia: I'll push the synthetic job and post the job id here once it's running. also adding a small ramp test to mimic ETL spikes.
sara: we should also log policy deltas in the incident channel for visibility.
matt: adding a checklist to the rollback runbook:
- revert commit
- push config
- check policy-manager pods
- validate: `sum(increase(api_responses_total{code=\"429\"}[5m]))` and `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))`
- confirm with support

alex: timeline to capture in postmortem: policy deploy 12:03 UTC, tickets + alerts 12:10-12:25, rollback decision 12:35, rollback complete 12:41, metrics stable 12:44.
deploy-bot: policy deploy revert finished at 12:41:10 UTC (status: success)
support-bot: billing ops confirmed credits applied for affected customers for window 12:03-12:44 UTC.
alex: thanks everyone. we'll schedule a quick follow-up to finalize the postmortem and safe rollout plan. closing thread when follow-ups created. :thumbsup:
